tagline: A small town below the Phu Phan range, Luang Pu Khao's Wat Tham Klong Phen, and the Ubolratana reservoir
introHtml: Nong Bua Lamphu is a small province in the upper Isan, bordering Udon Thani, Khon Kaen, and Loei. Most people just drive through on the way to Loei or Udon, but if you actually stop you'll find a quiet, easygoing town with a fair bit to see. In the center, the Shrine of King Naresuan the Great is the heart of the city, sitting next to the lotus pond (nong bua) that gave the province its name. To the west, the Phu Phan Kham ridge runs along the Ubolratana Dam reservoir, where you can sit, eat fish, and catch the breeze. For temple lovers, Wat Tham Klong Phen is where the revered monk Luang Pu Khao once spent the rains retreat. Nong Bua Lamphu works for nature, for temples, and for stopping off to eat homestyle Isan food along the way.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, good for heading up Phu Phan Kham for reservoir views and visiting temples. In the rainy season around June–September the waterfalls run and the rice fields turn green

highlights.name: Wat Tham Klong Phen
highlights.blurb: A forest temple tucked into the hills where Luang Pu Khao Analayo once spent the rains retreat, with a museum of his belongings and rock caves to walk through. A place of worship for the whole province.

highlights.name: Shrine of King Naresuan the Great
highlights.blurb: The shrine at the heart of town that locals hold dear, set beside the lotus pond that gave the province its name. It has an annual festival and a steady stream of people stopping to pay respects.

highlights.name: Phu Phan Kham and the Ubolratana reservoir
highlights.blurb: The Phu Phan Kham ridge runs along the Ubolratana Dam reservoir, with viewpoints over the wide water and the line of hills. This is the province's standout for nature.

highlights.name: Phu Kao–Phu Phan Kham National Park
highlights.blurb: A two-mountain park with oddly shaped rocks, prehistoric rock paintings, and viewpoints over the reservoir. Good for short hikes and camping.

highlights.name: Nong Bua, in the town center
highlights.blurb: The large pond in the middle of town that the province is named after. People come to walk, exercise, and sit by the water in the evening. It's the city's spot to unwind.

highlights.name: Local woven and mud-dyed cloth
highlights.blurb: Weaving villages around the province sell cotton and naturally mud-dyed cloth right where it's made. It's the handmade souvenir of Nong Bua Lamphu.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and bamboo-shoot soup, bold and proper Isan, found in every district. It's the daily meal for people in Nong Bua Lamphu.

foodScene.name: Grilled fish and waterside food
foodScene.note: Around the Ubolratana reservoir and Phu Phan Kham there are spots for grilled fish, steamed fish, and tom yum fish, easy to eat with the breeze by the water.

foodScene.name: Khao piak sen and Vietnamese kuay jap
foodScene.note: Being right next to Udon Thani, you'll find khao piak sen and Vietnamese-style kuay jap around town. A hot, brothy breakfast.

foodScene.name: Foraged greens and local vegetables
foodScene.note: In the rainy season the districts near the hills bring mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and local vegetables to market, for curries and dipping with nam phrik, homestyle.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) joints are spread all over town, a popular dinner that people gather for in groups, especially on weekends.

foodScene.name: Khao ji and local sweets
foodScene.note: Egg-coated grilled sticky rice (khao ji), khao tom mat, and other local sweets are found at the morning markets, cheap snacks and souvenirs.

foodScene.name: Night-market street food
foodScene.note: The evening market in town has grilled and fried snacks and desserts to graze on after dark, at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee in town
foodScene.note: Several new cafes have opened in town, good for a coffee break before heading out to temples or up the mountains.

attractions.name: Wat Tham Klong Phen
attractions.blurb: A forest temple tucked into the hills where Luang Pu Khao once spent the rains retreat, with a museum of his belongings and large rock caves to walk through, shaded by forest and boulders.

attractions.name: Phu Kao–Phu Phan Kham National Park
attractions.blurb: A two-mountain park with oddly shaped rocks, prehistoric paintings on the cave walls, and viewpoints over the Ubolratana reservoir.

attractions.name: Ubolratana Dam reservoir, Phu Phan Kham side
attractions.blurb: A wide stretch of water along the Phu Phan Kham ridge, with viewpoints and waterside restaurants, where you can catch the breeze and photograph the hills reflected in the water.

attractions.name: Shrine of King Naresuan the Great
attractions.blurb: The shrine at the heart of town that locals hold dear, with an annual ceremony and people stopping to pay respects throughout the day.

attractions.name: Nong Bua
attractions.blurb: The large pond in the middle of town that the province is named after, with a waterside path for exercising and sitting out in the evening.

attractions.name: Thao To Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A small waterfall near town that flows over rock platforms in the rainy season. Locals like to come to play in the water and picnic on weekends.

attractions.name: Luang Pu Khao Analayo Museum
attractions.blurb: A museum at Wat Tham Klong Phen that keeps Luang Pu Khao's belongings and tells the story of this revered forest-tradition monk.

attractions.name: Phu Pha Ya, prehistoric rock-painting site
attractions.blurb: A cliff in the Phu Kao area with paintings of people and animals thousands of years old. You walk up to see them along with views over the wide fields below.
